- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 66.97 → 68.21 or 68.02 → 69.41), then undercorrects.
- Underestimates in the final 5–10 days of forecast, particularly when true values show strong upward momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: model holds onto high forecasts longer than actual price tends to revert.
- Lagged response: model reacts to recent history with delay — e.g., 30-day history doesn’t fully capture short-term volatility.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the middle of the 30-day window (days 10–20), suggesting model struggles with mid-term momentum.
- When history shows strong downward trend, model often fails to adjust downward sufficiently — underestimates true drop.
- High volatility periods (e.g., 65–70 range) lead to overconfidence in model, resulting in higher-than-actual peaks.
